findings.title: Date overrides bypass busy checks, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not excluded by the override, the function returns true at line 133 before running the busy.every conflict check. This means calendar bookings and existing Cal bookings for that host are ignored on any day with a date override, so a slot can be offered even when the host is already busy. This applies to fixed hosts and regular non-team event hosts, leading to double-bookings on override days.

findings.title: Working-hours end time is computed from slot start, not slot end
findings.body: The working-hours validation sets both start and end to slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(). The end value should be derived from slotEndTime or at least start + eventLength. As written, a slot that starts inside the host's working hours but ends after the working-hours end passes the check. If the fixed host has shorter availability than the aggregate availability used to generate slots, bookings can be made outside that host's actual working hours.

findings.title: Zero-length date override check compares Dayjs objects with ===
findings.body: The condition dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes") compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. A zero-length date override used to mark a date unavailable does not block a slot that starts exactly at that override time, because the callback returns undefined and dateOverrideExist then returns true.

findings.title: Multiple same-day date overrides are not all considered
findings.body: The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately when it finds a same-day override that does not contain the slot. If a host has several date-override intervals on the same date, a slot that lies in a later interval is rejected because an earlier same-day interval returned true first. The logic should determine whether the slot is inside any of the same-day overrides rather than stopping at the first one that excludes it.

findings.title: Timezone-adjusted date overrides drop day-crossing information
findings.body: The active-override filter at line 206 still uses dayjs.utc(override.start), and the start/end calculation at lines 219-224 only keeps hour() and minute() after adding the offset. When the organizer/invitee timezone adjustment crosses midnight, this discards the new day. For example, a 23:30-23:45 Honolulu override is 02:30-02:45 next day in Los Angeles, but the current code can attach the override to the previous invitee day and produce 02:30 without carrying into the next day. This makes date overrides near midnight appear on the wrong day in certain timezones.

findings.title: No regression test for fixed-host date overrides in round-robin
findings.body: The PR's main round-robin fix is that fixed-host date overrides are now enforced in availableTimeSlots through checkIfIsAvailable, but the only added test covers a personal event date override with a different timezone. There is no test creating a round-robin event with one fixed host, a date override for that fixed host, and a round-robin host. That is the most complex new path and should have a regression test.
